articles.title: Colts’ Shane Steichen Reveals Unusual Post-London Plan
articles.summary: All good coaches have a plan when it comes to being strategic with schedules. A 17-game season can really be strenuous on the players' bodies and minds. This...
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts escaped London, England with a convincing 30-13 victory. The Washington Commanders were no match for Shane Steichen's seemingly prepared group. Following the matchup, both teams will turn around right away to play in Week 5. The NFL gives franchises options to select a bye after a game overseas, but neither did in this case. For the Colts, traveling to play a 2-2 Pittsburgh Steelers group will be a hostile challenge.

One interesting tidbit to mention is that Pittsburgh will be coming off of a Thursday Night Football showdown against the Cleveland Browns. This leads to quite a bit of rest while Indianapolis is in the opposite corner.

All good coaches have a plan when it comes to being strategic with schedules. A 17-game season can really be strenuous on the players' bodies and minds. This is why Steichen came up with a unique plan. He wanted to combat some of these challenges.

Colts Were Mindful Of Interesting Travel Disadvantage

Not only did Indianapolis have to travel back from London; but, the organization won't even have a home contest upon returning. Steichen spoke with the media on Wednesday and gave an in-depth look at the approach he and his staff took.

"We looked into that, sports performance stuff. Obviously, we want to make sure our guys are fresh going into this game," Steichen said. "[The Steelers] had 10 days, we'll have six. We gave them some good rest Monday, Tuesday and then obviously adjusting some of the practice stuff to make sure we're fresh and ready to go for Sunday."

There came a time when the Colts had to decide if rest or early preparation was more important heading into the Steelers game. Clearly, Steichen wanted the locker room to take a couple of days off to freshen up.

It would be understandable to call this disadvantage unfair. Pittsburgh will be rested up. However, Indianapolis could have easily decided to take a bye in Week 5. Now, the matchup will show if that would have been the right decision or not.

Indianapolis Looking To Get To Above .500

After an 0-2 start, there were some murmurings about things going south for the Colts. Since then, the collective has reeled the season back in. It would be a big result if a win against the Steelers ends up happening. Not only would it be an AFC victory, but Steichen and Co. would improve to 3-2.

One other key fact to mention here is that the NFL didn't do the Colts any favors. Their bye isn't until the first week in December. Even if things go right in Pittsburgh, Indianapolis isn't going to get much time off for a couple of months.

articles.title: Spanish legend issues stark warning to Real Madrid over title race: ‘If Barça continues like this, it’s impossible’
articles.summary: With the Ballon d’Or race heating up ahead of the ceremony in London later this month, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane have emerged as the two main candidates. I...
articles.body:
With the Ballon d'Or race heating up ahead of the ceremony in London later this month, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane have emerged as the two main candidates.

In a recent interaction with COPE, though, Spanish football legend David Silva has backed Fabian Ruiz to win the Ballon d'Or for his excellent performances for Spain and PSG.

In the same interview, Silva also talked about the La Liga title race, notably issuing a stark warning to Real Madrid.

When asked about the title race, Silva offered his view as to whether or not Real Madrid can catch up with Barcelona, with the club already trailing the Catalans by six points.

David Silva believes it will be difficult to stop Barcelona. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

The former Man City superstar noted that it will be difficult for Real Madrid to keep up if Barcelona continue their current run of form.

"If Barça continues like this, it's impossible," he said (h/t Mundo Deportivo ).

They're playing at a very high level and have been playing very well for several years now with this coach, and they've strengthened their squad very well. If they continue at this level, they'll have no rivals."

Barcelona have indeed look unstoppable this season, winning all their matches while scoring goals for fun.

Can Mourinho's team bounce back after the break? (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images)

That being said, Silva reminded everyone that Real Madrid should never be ruled out, as they have a tendency to always bounce back.

"You can never count them out because they have great players and if they stay close until the end of the league, they can fight," he said.

But the Spaniard concluded by stating that Barcelona, at this level, will be very difficult to stop, even if Real Madrid manage to maintain a winning form.

"But I insist, if Barça continues at this level, I don't think so, " he concluded.

Silva's comments come just ahead of the resumption of club football, with Real Madrid slated to take on Villarreal this weekend, a game where coach Jose Mourinho will face a severe shortage of centre-backs and could be forced to make some unwanted changes.

articles.body:
St. Louis CITY SC put their 17-game league unbeaten run on the line against the LA Galaxy during Matchday 29's Sunday Night Soccer presented by Continental Tire matchup.

St. Louis kept their unbeaten streak alive, earning a 3-0 road victory over Red Bull New York .

Star striker Rafael Navarro opened the scoring after five minutes, then Simon Becher and Tomáš Ostrák added late insurance tallies to secure the win.

Rafael Navarro: St. Louis CITY's biggest summer signing has made an immediate impact, netting five goals in five games since arriving in a blockbuster trade with the Colorado Rapids.

Carlo Holse: The Danish international has quickly settled into his new surroundings, contributing 3g/2a in nine MLS matches since joining from the Turkish Süper Lig.

Simon Becher: Although St. Louis added plenty of attacking talent during the summer transfer window, Becher is the team leader in goal contributions (9g/5a).

Roman Bürki: The 2023 MLS Goalkeeper of the Year has helped St. Louis allow the sixth-fewest goals (36) league-wide this year.

St. Louis have authored a remarkable turnaround under first-year head coach Yoann Damet, going unbeaten in 17 straight league matches and 19 across all competitions.

They're one game away from tying Red Bull New York for the all-time unbeaten run across all competitions (20 games; 2016 season).

Aside from challenging for first place in the Western Conference, St. Louis have also reached the US Open Cup final. They'll visit the Columbus Crew on Oct. 21 and vie for the club's first-ever trophy.

The Galaxy rallied from two goals down to win 3-2 at home over the Colorado Rapids .

LA benefited from a Reggie Cannon own goal before João Klauss equalized in the 66th minute. Justin Haak completed the comeback eight minutes later, heading home his first Galaxy goal.

Sergi Roberto: The former FC Barcelona midfielder has brought class and calm to the Galaxy lineup since arriving from Como in Italy's Serie A.

After spending much of the year below the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs line, LA look to be finding form at the right time. The Galaxy are unbeaten in three games and recently earned galvanizing victories over Minnesota United FC and Colorado.

Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone has been called up to the England squad for their forthcoming World Cup play-off games with Greece.

The 27-year-old was originally left out of Sarina Wiegman's 23-player squad , which was announced last week but will now join up with the group following a minor injury to Lucy Bronze .

Toone was omitted alongside fellow England regular Chloe Kelly and Wiegman later stated she "expected more" from the pair.

Speaking at St George's Park at the time of the initial squad announcement, Wiegman told a press conference: "The levels weren't what I expect from them on the pitch and I've had a conversation with them and there's big competition going on too.

"It has been a really hard decision for both of them. I really believe in them and we follow them really well and we expect a bit more and know they can bring more.

"I hope they can step up and show what they can do because I'm convinced they can do better. They took the feedback well, in a positive way, but it is also hard to take. It is not a nice message.

"I hope they respond on it really well. I hope they come back even better than they were before."

Toone has only completed 90 minutes for Manchester United once this campaign under new boss Eva Olid.

Bronze played for Chelsea in their 3-0 victory over West Ham but sustained an injury which means she will now return to her club for further assessment.

The Lionesses arrived in Crete on Wednesday ahead of Friday's first leg play-off with Greece at the Pankritio Stadium. The second leg is at Leicester's King Power Stadium on Tuesday.
